OK so yes I'd recommend it but it has a few issues.  I'm going to list them because I have workarounds I figured out. I really do enjoy the game, it's silly. If you like the two point games you should definitely enjoy this one. 

Here are some of the things I found work arounds for/find kinda annoying. Not bad enough to rage quit or stop enjoying the game, but annoying. 
* Patients get stuck
Every now and then you'll get a warning with a frownie face saying a patient is getting upset. And so far every time I see that it's because they're stuck. (It's supposed to be if the lines are too long and there's no food etc.) But if you try to make them first in line, hand them a machine etc. They just stand there frozen. If you exit to the menu and come back they start moving. It's rather annoying especially since it happened so many times.
* Level 3 Mission
There's a weird issue with level three, you have to treat some specific patients and somehow after you treat them all the mission doesn't complete.  This one I had to exit the game and launch it again and then the mission popped up again, I completed it and it worked. 
* Doctors staying unassigned
So you have rooms and you assign doctors to them. But sometimes you move things around. At one point it seemed to work, if a room didn't have a doctor (one went on break or whatever) another doctor would fill in. (You can lock doctors to rooms so they won't fill in elsewhere etc. But I'm referring to unassigned doctors.)
Usually this works. But I've had a few times where I had rooms needing doctors and my doctors are milling about. 
* Can't turn off research
If you have a research room up to three of your doctors will go in the room and do research.  Other rooms you can "turn off" when you don't want it active but you can't turn off the research room. Downside is you may have three doctors doing research and have rooms that have lines going out the door waiting for the doctor.  So I end up having to delete it so they stop getting stuck there. So far I'm not really seeing a massive benefit of the research room but if you have a good income coming in you can afford the extra doctors.

I've played this game obsessively, and I have a fair amount to say. I will keep the short review here at the top. It is as follows:

This game is very fun and has a good brand of humor. If you like the first mission, you'll enjoy the rest of the game. It has glitches and bugs, but only really shows them after extended play and don't majorly impact the experience much. If you can tolerate that, this game's great, would highly recommend.

For the longer form review, I have attempted to 100% this game in challenge mode, and had to give up on it because of the lengthy list of bugs and other issues I've run into the game for longer play. The base game story had barely any issues, it was well made and funny, with a heartwarming... Mostly heartwarming story and had a good feel to it, even if it was a tad on the easy side after level two. 

The main trouble begins with sandbox missions or missions with large patient counts. To state the numerous glitches I've endured would take a length of time and text, so I will summarize by saying that I've had the research system (vital for making your life easier) bug out on me every other mission, I've had text glitch in the compendium and ruin the very fun stories by repeating entries or making it unclear if the messages are as intended, or simply glitched out. I've had objects I was attempting to place vanish from existence, still extant in that I could see the various patients and doctors use them but I could no longer move them. I'm unsure if something has broken as computers have advanced and left this game a little in the dust, but it's been a frustrating experience trying to wrangle the game into the 'perfect' state for me to actually complete all of the objectives I want to.

The game suffers from performance issues with enough patients, even with a fairly sturdy rig. This can be mitigated with the research system, if you manage to get it to work, but otherwise performance issues were not a major concern. I say this because it took me managing to put 500 patients per 5 minute cycle through my hospital before the performance actually tanked, and then it became almost unplayable. The difference will happen immediately, and can usually be avoided. 

Aside from that, I have very few complaints. Despite the usual hurdles of these games and ensuring people move to where you need them, it's actually fairly easy to maneuver patients and doctors around even if assigning them and keeping track of who goes where can be a bit maddening. I have no complaints about the gameplay itself, watching things fill up and watching patients get treated is a very zen experience, helped by the muted but still very good soundtrack. The only discomfort I have is that, in sandbox, many of the special events tend to lock themselves in a repeat loop of a very small number, meaning it's going to get very boring very quickly when you hit all of your 'available' missions.

I also have not played the DLC. I can't comment on it whatsoever.

One of my top 5 games of all time is Theme Hospital. I understand most people probably got 20 hours out of that title, but I sank about 300 hours into playing and min/maxing the everloving heck out of Theme Hospital (and then Two Point Hospital, its rightful heir) so that's my cred for this review.

I played the first two story scenarios and was impressed with the visuals, the polish, the voice acting, the vibe, etc. But wasn't instantly hooked. After the third scenario, something clicked and I understood the bigger picture, and the game's expectations for how many of each type of room to build in response to an influx of patients, and can say this one gets a thumbs up from me. It's just similar enough to scratch the itch I miss from Theme/TwoPoint Hospital, and just new enough to keep me glued to the screen.

I'm recommending this game after 16 hours, even though I probably won't play it any more. The story bits are fun, it looks great, there is a lot to like. But the game play feels a bit underwhelming. I guess I would hope for more interactions between the various rooms, clinicians, disease, etc. But mostly the game play seems to be "if you don't have enough of room x, build more room x". It doesn't grip me the way I feel like it should, like how Oxygen Not Included or Mind over Magic grip me. 

I find some bits need more micromanaging that I would like. Like, making recovery wards and pest traps seem to me they should be a more reliable way to manage patients whose health is dropping rapidly or pests coming in. But neither seems to really work well, you still have to personally target many pests for elimination and use the health potions on a lot of individual patients. Maybe I'm doing something wrong? I'll accept that is possible. 

It's a good game to get on sale, I think.

Sketching out my own walls lets me see and create a flow for patients more easily than surprise this room is 3x4 and this is 4x4 and this is 3x3 so you're going to need to play tetris or have an awkward bit sticking out that impacts the flow of your hallways. It's okay to venture off the beaten path or even offer both paths when we have put another 25 or 30 years of experience in design and controls on top of the classics.

I've played through all the story missions and gotten the 5 star achievs for each, but have yet to tackle most of the challenge modes and side missions.

It's entertaining, doesn't take itself too seriously, and the price is reasonable. I thought the story was funny--and it's fully voiced albeit unrepentantly campy. I looked up some of the VAs and at least some appear to be the creators of the game doing the voice work in-house--well I couldn't tell, so they did a pretty good job. 

If you like lore, there's a fair bit of it in all the different diseases you can research and leveling that up gives you more tidbits. 

Game has good quality of life features like overlays, room templates, performance charts, etc. but you don't need to engage too heavily with these systems or do math to play, it's there to help you optimize. 

If you like aesthetic features, there are tons of unlockable 'decorations' that improve patient mood. You can customize room colors too.

I only have two negative comments: First, there is a certain 'sameness' to the build order/strategy, but I think that's something all of these types of games struggle to overcome. More notably, assigning staff to rooms can be a frustrating process as they tend to move around without your permission. There is a "lock" button to force them to a specific room and ban anyone else from taking the slot; it usually works, but not always. Sometimes you'll come back 10 minutes later and find the assignments changed. I believe this system is intended to help optimize your workforce and relieve micro burden (for instance, if you have too many doctors of a certain specialty, the game will assign the idle ones to fill in for empty rooms you don't have any doctors for) so it's not all bad, it just sometimes has wonky logic that fails to respect a manually set override by the player. As annoying as this is, however, I don't think it is a serious enough issue to factor in a decision to purchase the game; it's merely a nuisance to be aware of.

Unlike some other reviewers, I did not encounter any crashes or serious technical issues. Did have a couple minor incidents, such as times patients got stuck and couldn't be moved, but reloading the save fixed any glitches I encountered.

Already got my money's worth and looking forward to trying the challenge modes and the DLC.

My new favourite hospital tycoon game. Or just favourite tycoon game period. Management layer is perfect grounding: everything works smoothly, you always know what's going on, what can you do and how. I was never disoriented, lost or betrayed by game acting differently from what I wanted. Even amidst hectic crises, only thing in the way of success was my very-much-possible mismanagement. From building to restructuring, from patients to doctors, everything you want to manage, can be done effortlessly (well you still need to think, mind) and game flows in steadily crisp tempo.

There's a lot of "cool" conditions to treat, specialized rooms to build, races with different traits to recruit from and so on. All this good stuff delivered with lovingly crafted, rich lore (each disease got its own substory to unlock through research, e. g.). Galacticare also has surprisingly good and gripping story with likeable characters. Elevated to pure joy by, I can't stress this enough, [b]excellent[/b] writing and voice acting. Galacticare is comedy first and foremost, but doesn't fall the wacky hole. It revels in intelligent understated humour and layered sarcasm in the best british-like way. Which is godly mana for me. Again, it's an admirable work of writers pouring big talent into this. And again, it's exquisitly delivered by actors.

There's nothing cheap, no cut corners here. On the contrary, it surprises only in positive ways. It feels almost unreal to find so polished game nowadays and it coheres with the amount of fun I had the whole time.

P. S. If you want to discover other less knows gems, you're welcome to visit my curator page: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45655021-Nods-for-Underdogs/]Nods for Underdogs[/url].

This game deserves a lot more love in my view - as has been said it's Theme Hospital in space but a slightly different take on the formula vs the original or Two Point. Less about managing different kinds of staff, more about the different species that come through your doors; less on diagnosis but more on multi-stage treatments; slightly lighter on mechanics but has a full-on story mode that's decently fleshed out (rather than just a campaign with themed levels).

Singling out two for criticism and one for praise - the challenge mode is too hard to be fun, and there are annoying bugs with patients becoming unresponsive and impossible to clear; but on the other hand this game seems to mostly avoid the gameplay ever feeling a bit stodgy, which is a near certainty in these kinds of games (much as I love them) - I think that's a real, rare achievement.

Aside from that he strengths and weaknesses of this game are mostly similar to its inspiration and its inspiration's other spiritual sequel - but it plays differently enough that it feels like a fresh experience. Highly recommended if you like this kind of game.

I am not, typically, a hospital sim fan as a rule, but with this being Brightrock, that didn't matter! I got exactly what I expected; a very enjoyable management game with that particular Brightrock humour.

As usual, top-notch work. It took me 71 hours to 5-star all the campaign missions, sandboxes and the expansion (which came out during the latter half of my playthrough). The campaign was both amusing and varied enough to keep my interest, though I had about had enough by the end. (Still that's 10-20 more hours than a typical RPG...!) I did not attempt the challenge mode difficulty; normal was a pleasant experience and enough for me. It was genuinely nice to play a game that didn't frustrate me for a change. I didn't quite 100% it - Brother Gumbo was still level 9 and I was only 92% towards maxing out the Khouber Bali species relationship; but at that point I'd have been doing it for the sake of it for a likely a fair few more hours. (Given as right up to the end of the last bit of sandbox, I will note I can't say I've even seen all sandbox repeatable quest, since the expansion clearly introduced some new ones, but I suspect I've seen the majority.)

The humour is all good, ranging from funny to some really laugh-out loud moments. The story itself is suitably light-hearted for the most part, though that last mission and expansion turn up the stakes and are slightly more serious (slightly...) 

The characters were all very strong, well-written an engaging, carried by the excellent voice-work. I particularly enjoyed the arc in the interactions between HEAL and MEDI. Of the consultants, I think the stongest characters were Twiggy, Alpha and Ohdious (the first two being among the best mechanically, I think, to me). It should also be noted that among the humour in the lore there was the expected level of world-building which showed serious,, non-comedic, genuine thought had gone into it, before the humour was layered on the top. I particularly approve of that.

The sound design was also very good; popping the critters, pests and chitters had a very satisfying splat.

I encountered a couple of minor bugs, but nothing that interrupted the play. 

I think my biggest gripe, if you can even call it that, is that I was usually so busy moving up and down, searching and popping critters, that I really had chance to sit back an appreciate the animations as well, unique for each treatment and disease.

Overall then, a very strong recommendation, and one i am not at all surprised to be making on a Brightrock game.

同样的厂商，上一作《地下城争夺战》，全成就了，依然继续玩了几百小时。很喜欢那款游戏。
现在这款游戏总体来讲还不错。但也有些影响游玩心情和体验的bug:
1，游戏偶尔会随机出现一个病人被固定在原地无法移动，无法踢出医院。它的属性会一点点降低，生命值直到归零依然固定在哪里。然后右下角就会提示一个病人心情很糟，一个病人需求很糟，一点查看追踪，就是这个bug人。目前我把这个内容发到官方，有个老哥在下面评论说通过读档来消除这个人物。但官方支援论坛在去年的时候就已经宣称这个bug在年底的时候已经通过更新修复了，但我现在是25年的4月份依然还会遇到这种情况，我也是服了。
2，之前已经全部关卡五星了，后来更新了一个挑战模式，对我感觉吸引力不太大，我也没有打，前两天开始从第一关开始挑战模式五星难度开玩，第一关打完拿到成就了，结果第二关就没拿到五星了依然不弹出成就，这真的很影响体验。我也不想再为了成就重新打这一次了。去官方论坛看了一下，好多人都在说。通关没有谈出成就这个问题。我想如果官方只是没办法完全解决这个bug的话，目前我是不太想玩儿这个游戏了。
以上就是比较影响体验的bug，其他的小bug像是人物头像错位这种不影响游戏体验，就无所谓了。
再说说游玩感想，总体没啥难度，就是多建前台，多建诊室，根据关卡任务来定制分配各种病症诊室，及时消化突如其来的大量病人，关注病人列表按生命值高低排序，血量最低，或者掉血速率快的人优先治疗，血量危急的直接手动加血，或者推送到疗养先加血。
关于房间建立，每个房间至少高于基本要求一排格子（比如要去3x3基本，但你可以做成4x3）这样才不会显示房间过于拥挤。为了满足个种族的喜好，每个房间要有至少要有各种装扮（比如两个灯泡，一个柜子，一两张贴纸，一个奇趣装扮，一两株花，一个窗户）这样的话每一个种族它的需求都会得到相应的满足。
每个诊室我的习惯是门口摆上小花盆，然后墙边顺着摆放小凳子，这样病人不会抱怨没有座位。
有条件的话走廊最好是三格宽度，不然有个种族总会嫌走廊或房间或者人多拥挤，看着其实挺烦的。
雇医生要看坏习惯只要不是什么随机致死病人，影响周围人的心情，以及拖慢治疗就行。什么喜欢吃东西或者上厕所，减少研发这些在我看来影响不大，好习惯是加速治疗时间和给病人加健康值。
垃圾桶这些最好辐射到就行，还有公厕，食物机这些，不过要注意垃圾桶，要放有一种介绍是可进食的那种垃圾桶，不然有一个种族要抱怨没有可以翻找进食的垃圾桶。
想做到五星其实也简单的，就是大量治疗病人和节省病人的等待时机，治疗好出院的生命值来评判。想提升病人入院的数量就摆几个异空间通道具体叫啥名字忘了，就是粉色的那个出口，不断有人从里面走出来，多摆那个要注意周边不要有太多障碍，不然人物会卡到。多放几个传送门，从前台到诊室到各个科室。
反正这个游戏感觉就是面多了加水，水多了加面。外星人会得各种各样的病症，这些病症的名称和病状看起来很搞笑。一些诊室的诊疗机器也特别能整活儿。有时候你观看各种病症的治疗，盯着一个人从诊室到治疗完成去疗养院这一系列的过程。都觉得很有趣，很搞笑。
但这个游戏我买了之后感觉他更新的不是很勤快。Dlc出了，但是在我看来吸引力不太大。然后游戏还有这些小bug影响游玩的心情，官方好像始终没有把这些bug完全处理干净。
如果10分是满分的话，我给这个游戏打8分。如果语音能像双点一样变成中文，我想他会更加分。

An enjoyable take on hospital sims which incorporates British humour. Every time I sat down and played a mission I really enjoyed it. You can tell a lot of passion was put into this game by developers and voice actors, nothing felt out of place and it was a good game to pick up every day or so and play through.

Patients here come from a range of species with each one requiring specific decorations in order to keep them happy. This can be windows, plants, benches or wide corridors. Whilst this is not really essential to completing most missions, if the player wants 5 stars then this will need to be considered. 

Conditions vary based on a danger scale. It is not overly hard to keep patients alive and death penalties of regular patients are not that harsh.

26 hours is just long enough to finish the base game with about half of the hospitals at 5 stars.

There is a storyline to Galacticare and each map involves a different challenge. This helps to keep the humour fresh as I find sometimes with Two Point I am muting the music and announcements as they repeat over and over.

I preferred curing people in Galacticare as opposed to Two Point as the diseases had some funny treatments. I watched each new room to see it function. I really enjoyed treating patients who had overslept by blowing crust off their bodies, hitting those who had permafrost with a flamethrower in Projectile Medicine and shrinking a spaceship to nanoscale and flying it into a patient. I preferred this humour to Two Point. Even the index of conditions was funny as more levels in researched revealed more details.

I liked how it was easy to add new rooms and doctors in case of a backlog and the game automatically assigned patients between them without further input from me. Teleportation pads to get people around the hospital quickly was a great amendment and I now miss this in other hospital sims.

There are some negatives. This game from what I have read launched in a similar condition to No Man's Sky. A lot of work has been put into this game and it is a labour of love, however I had the occasional patient bug out and get stuck (fixed by a restart), graphical glitches of doors remaining open and a consultant not teleporting to where she should. Some of these have been fixed in the latest patch however some still remain.

Overall I really enjoyed this game and after the first 15 hours I have purchased all DLC and War for the Overworld which were both made by this developer. I do not see myself returning to Two Point after playing this.
